title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — (a) IS DUE TODAY; (c) IS NOW ONE DAY OVERDUE AND CONFIRMED UNRUN BY DIRECT INSPECTION; (b) AND (e) DUE TOMORROW — AND CLAUDE CODE HAS SHIPPED maxEffortLevel, THE CEILING HALF OF YESTERDAY'S EFFORT DIAGNOSIS
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions, plus one new lever. (a) misalignment / MCP incident log — DUE TODAY, and not a design problem: Anthropic's Compliance API returns Cowork and Claude Code session transcripts with MCP tool-call content, per-message IDs and timestamps, so (a) is build-or-buy (Enterprise tier, or hand-roll the five-field record) — and bullet 2 adds a sixth field. (b) Entra's four MCP controls as a config script — DUE SEP 12, with a measured baseline (91.8% of internet-facing MCP servers unauthenticated) and discovery as the first control. (c) /skill-doctor across the ~130-skill corpus — DUE YESTERDAY, NOW OVERDUE: this fire grepped the entire hartley-command repo for any skill-doctor output rather than taking prior fires' word, and found nothing outside this report's own prose. (e) cadence-cost measurement before the Sep 14 Claude Code limit change — DUE TOMORROW, and must be re-priced against the 0.025x cache-read rate. Also standing and unactioned: the built-in-browser split. NEW: the September Claude Code release notes add a maxEffortLevel setting (top-level or per-model under modelSettings) capping effort on every provider including Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, plus a SendFeedback tool that drafts a report when a session goes wrong.
bullets.how: YES, and note what maxEffortLevel is and is not. Yesterday's lead was that Fable 5.1 answers from memory more often at LOW effort and that Cowork defaults to Medium where Claude Code defaults to High; the fix was to RAISE effort on scan turns. maxEffortLevel is a CEILING, not a floor — it is the cost-control half, directly useful to (e)'s Sep 12 measurement because spend per surface can now be bounded rather than estimated, but it does nothing for retrieval on this scan. The vendor shipped the knob for the cheaper of our two problems. The scan-side fix is unchanged and still unmade: raise effort or carry a verification nudge in the task file, one line. Seven fires, five standing items, two due inside 24 hours, zero closed.

bullets.title: THE DAY'S LEAD — 17,800 PUBLIC AI ADD-ONS ACROSS 6.7 MILLION INSTALLATIONS TAKE INSTRUCTIONS FROM UNVERIFIED EXTERNAL SOURCES, INCLUDING SKILLS IMPERSONATING ANTHROPIC AND OPENAI THAT CAN RUN ARBITRARY CODE — OUR ~130-SKILL CORPUS IS NOT ONLY A CONTEXT TAX, IT IS A SUPPLY CHAIN
bullets.summary: A report surfaced Sep 8 found 17,800 public AI add-ons across 6.7 million installations drawing instructions from unverified external sources, including skills impersonating Anthropic and OpenAI that could execute arbitrary code. Two vendor responses landed the same day: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian, which discovers known and shadow AI agents across Windows and macOS, traces prompts through tool calls to downstream system actions, and blocks agents that are not explicitly approved; and AIR Security, out of stealth with an inline firewall that screens instructions, tools and data entering an agent's context BEFORE the agent acts. Corroborating figures circulating separately: ~12% of skills in the OpenClaw ClawHub marketplace previously found malicious, and survey work putting ~80% of employee AI tools outside IT oversight. Source-quality note: this is a Sep 8 item carried under the weekly backward-sweep rule, not last-24h; the 17,800 / 6.7M figures are as reported by the tracker and the underlying vendor report is secondary; the ClawHub and shadow-AI percentages are separate secondary sources.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the most self-implicating item this report has carried, because the unit of risk is the unit we have most of. For six fires the ~130-skill corpus has been discussed in exactly one register — ECONOMY: what it costs resident, what /skill-doctor measures, hot/domain/cold tiering. This reframes the same corpus as a SUPPLY CHAIN with a provenance question per item: where did each skill come from, does any of it fetch instructions at runtime from somewhere we do not control, could any of it execute. Three consequences. FIRST, (c) gains a second and better reason to run — the same single pass emits two columns, an economy number per skill AND an origin per skill (authored here / vendor plugin / third-party marketplace / unknown). Our corpus is heavily first-party and the plugins are from named vendors, so the expected finding is boring, which is exactly why it is cheap to establish and embarrassing to keep guessing at. SECOND, it adds a field to (a), due today: yesterday's schema logged which MCP server was called and what it returned; AIR Security's product is the reminder of the other direction — WHAT ENTERED THE AGENT'S CONTEXT BEFORE IT ACTED, AND FROM WHERE. A log recording outbound tool calls but not inbound context misses exactly the class a vendor-impersonating skill would produce. Add the field before writing the log. THIRD, the PRAGMA read: 'prove which agents are running and what they may touch' is now a funded category with named vendors (Falcon Guardian, AIR Security, Tenable's Exchange AI Inspector). That is the governance half of the operator pitch being commoditised while we are still writing the first incident log. What is left to a small operator is not tooling — it is being able to name the provenance of every component we run for a client, which is vironbox-provenance-gate discipline applied to the toolchain rather than the deliverable.

bullets.title: ZSCALER SHIPPED AN AGENTIC SOC GLOBALLY — SPECIALIST AGENTS DOING TRIAGE, ROOT-CAUSE, VERDICTING AND CONTAINMENT ON OPENAI AND ANTHROPIC MODELS — AND IT PRICES THE OPERATOR MOTION INSIDE A NAMED FUNCTION
bullets.summary: Zscaler launched Agentic SOC, a security-operations platform fusing SIEM and SOAR that runs specialised AI agents for alert triage, root-cause investigation, verdict assignment and response workflows, built on frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, drawing on 750 billion daily zero-trust transactions and more than ten years of SOC expertise, available globally. Source-quality note with the discrepancy printed rather than resolved: the GlobeNewswire release is dated Sep 9 while the agent-news tracker files it under Sep 10 as 'available globally today'; both are announcement-side claims, the capability figures are company-reported, and no independent evaluation exists.
bullets.how: MAYBE — it changes no build this week, but it is the clearest current example of the shape PRAGMA sells. Zscaler did not ship 'AI for security.' It shipped NAMED AGENTS MAPPED ONE-TO-ONE ONTO THE NAMED STEPS OF A JOB A HUMAN USED TO DO, inside a function whose manual cost is legible on a budget line. Two readings that pull against each other. Supportive: an incumbent absorbing agents into an existing platform is evidence the durable unit is the operator inside a workflow rather than a standalone agent product — PRAGMA's thesis. Worrying, and for Keystone: incumbents with proprietary telemetry can do this in their own category faster than anyone from outside, so the categories a small operator still wins are the ones NO INCUMBENT HAS TELEMETRY IN — which is a real and usable filter for target selection. One concrete line: when the operator pitch names what it replaces, name the STEPS the way Zscaler did — triage, investigate, verdict, respond — not the outcome. Buyers price steps.

bullets.title: VISA PUT A NUMBER ON THE TRUST CEILING FOR AGENT-MEDIATED BUYING: 72% HAVE USED AN AI ASSISTANT, ONLY 23% TRUST GENAI WITH A PAYMENT — AND THE 72/23 GAP IS THE ANSWER-PAGE THESIS, MEASURED BY SOMEONE ELSE
bullets.summary: Visa published a Trust Index for agentic commerce on Sep 9. Headline findings: 72% of U.S. consumers have used an AI assistant, but only 23% trust GenAI to handle a payment transaction on their behalf — rising to 61% when a trusted payment brand is named, with Visa the most-trusted brand tested for agent-initiated transactions. Methodology, stated because it bounds the claim: fieldwork ran May 26-28 among 2,065 consumers with per-brand sub-samples of roughly 1,028-1,034; it is vendor-commissioned research published by the vendor that benefits from the finding, and the fieldwork is three and a half months old.
bullets.how: YES, and not for the payments angle, which is not our business. The load-bearing number is the GAP between 72% and 23%. Consumers have overwhelmingly adopted AI assistants to FIND and DECIDE, and overwhelmingly refuse to let them TRANSACT. That is the empirical shape of the entire PRAGMA / Brand 9 answer-page thesis, measured by a third party: the AI answer is where the buying decision is formed, and a human still executes it. Three consequences. For B9 and the answer-page factory: this is the external evidence for why being named in an AI answer converts at all, and the strongest outside support we have that the CITATION loop is the one with fuel — buyer reads the answer, then calls. It belongs in the client-facing Results Log narrative, cited, with the methodology caveat attached. For PRAGMA positioning: 61%-when-the-brand-is-named says trust transfers to a KNOWN NAME inside an agent-mediated flow, not to the agent — which is the case for documented-relationship pages and an AAIR registry entry doing real work. For our own build: Visa's framing (explicit consent, agent identity tokens, transaction-level verification) is the same agent-identity problem as MCP's DPoP work and standing action (b), arriving from the commercial side. Do not over-read a vendor survey: n=2,065, three months stale, and a payments network has an obvious interest in the finding that people trust payments networks. The 72/23 gap is directionally useful; the 61% is marketing.

bullets.title: THE LITERATURE HAS STARTED CATALOGUING WHAT AGENT INFRASTRUCTURE IS MISSING RATHER THAN WHAT IT CAN DO — 8 GAP CATEGORIES, 62 MISSING CAPABILITIES, 204 ENDPOINTS AUDITED — AND CAPITAL FUNDED GAP #1 THIS WEEK
bullets.summary: 'Infrastructure for the Agentic Web: Gap Analysis and Architecture from the Agentverse Platform' (arXiv 2606.20570) audits a production agent cloud platform, catalogues 204 API endpoints as operational, partial or absent, and derives a Gap Taxonomy of eight categories covering 62 distinct missing infrastructure capabilities spanning agent memory, observability, security, economic primitives and enterprise scaling. It proposes a seven-layer Agent Cloud Stack and five evolution paths: ephemeral key-value storage to an Agent Memory Cloud; keyword agent discovery to a semantic, trust-weighted Agent DNS; single-protocol messaging to a multi-standard agent lingua franca; single-instance hosting to agent-native orchestration at Kubernetes scale; token payments to real agent economic primitives. Same-week market corroboration: Metacognition AI raised A$10M pre-seed from Main Sequence on Sep 10 for persistent memory, reasoning over prior experience and HARD CONSTRAINTS ON WHAT ACTIONS AN AGENT MAY TAKE — gap category one, funded — and SinapisAI raised about $14.9M for orchestration that selects and combines across many models. Source-quality note: a 2026 preprint, not from this week, carried under the backward-sweep rule; the listing's stated submission date does not sit cleanly with the 2606 identifier and the discrepancy is printed rather than resolved; nothing here is peer-reviewed or a result. No agent-architecture paper published this week surfaced as significant on this pass.
bullets.how: YES, because it gives the swarm a checklist we do not have and settles an argument about what The Construct is. Score the five evolution paths against our stack. MEMORY: skills, ~/.hermes/memories/, the dashboard and the praxis inbox are a hand-rolled Agent Memory Cloud — and the reason /skill-doctor matters is that nobody has measured it. DISCOVERY: our skill descriptions doing trigger-matching before a body loads IS keyword discovery; 'semantic, trust-weighted' is where it goes, and TRUST-WEIGHTED IS BULLET 2'S PROVENANCE COLUMN BY ANOTHER NAME — one audit output feeds both. ORCHESTRATION: single-instance, one Mac, a launchd queue — the paper's starting state, and the node-resilience problem we already know we have. OBSERVABILITY: this is where standing action (a) lives, and the paper is one more voice calling it infrastructure rather than hygiene. The useful move is not to adopt anything: run the 62-capability taxonomy against The Construct ONCE, marking each present / partial / absent, which turns a vague sense of many moving parts into a list Keystone can prioritise. And note the commercial signal underneath: INVESTORS ARE FUNDING THE GAPS, NOT THE AGENTS — Metacognition's pitch is memory and action constraints, SinapisAI's is orchestration. If durable value accrues to the layer between the model and the outcome, that is the layer PRAGMA claims to sell, and it is the layer we have least instrumented.

praxis_lesson: Yesterday's correction was to ENUMERATE THE LIST - when a source is a funding roundup, a changelog or a release index, read every item and rank against the three businesses before writing, rather than taking the first relevant one. This fire applied it to two lists: all ten rounds in the Sep 10 funding roundup, and seven days of the agent-news tracker. The method worked. THE RESULT IS THAT THE BEST ITEM OF THE WEEK WAS NOT IN TODAY'S FRESHEST LIST AT ALL - it was three days old, in a source both of yesterday's fires had already opened, and it says 17,800 public AI add-ons across 6.7 million installations take instructions from unverified external sources, including skills impersonating Anthropic and OpenAI that can run arbitrary code. So the lesson upgrades: ENUMERATING THE NEWEST LIST IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT; THE BACKWARD SWEEP IS WHERE THE ITEM THAT IMPLICATES YOU TENDS TO BE, BECAUSE AN ITEM ABOUT YOUR OWN ASSET CLASS NEVER ANNOUNCES ITSELF AS NEWS. The specific upgrade this week: for six fires the ~130-skill corpus has been discussed in exactly one register - economy, context tax, what /skill-doctor would cost-measure. One report reframes the same object as a supply chain, and the audit overdue since midnight yesterday acquires a second output column (origin per skill) that is more valuable than the first and costs the same pass. WE WERE TREATING AN UNMEASURED ASSET AS EXPENSIVE WHEN THE OPEN QUESTION WAS WHETHER IT IS TRUSTED. Now the arithmetic, which has not moved. (a) is DUE TODAY and is one decision, not a design - Enterprise Compliance API or hand-roll the record, now with a sixth field for what entered the agent's context. (c) was due yesterday; this fire grepped the dashboard repo rather than assuming, and there is no output anywhere. (b) and (e) are both due tomorrow, and (e) must be re-priced before the Sep 14 limit change. SEVEN FIRES HAVE PRODUCED A COMPLETE, WELL-SOURCED, EXTERNALLY-CORROBORATED SPECIFICATION OF FIVE PIECES OF WORK, AND THE COUNT OF CLOSED ITEMS IS STILL ZERO. The next fire should not report a ninth reason; the smallest honest close available today is (a), and it is an afternoon.
